facebook.long_form:
*Window: 8:00 AM MT*

If you haven't started planning your weekend yet, here's the plan: Pikes Peak Regional Airshow, September 19 and 20 at Colorado Springs Airport.

Gates open at 8:30 AM. The airshow performances run from 10:50 AM to 2:25 PM both days. You're looking at WWII warbirds, a B-17 Flying Fortress, P-47 Thunderbolt, Corsair, B-25 Mitchell, and a live F-35 demo piloted by Kristin "Beo" Wolfe. Plus ground displays, kid zones, veteran recognition, and aviation exhibits your kids can actually explore up close.

Ticket pricing: adults are $53.20, kids ages 4 to 12 are $42.18, and children 3 and under get in free. Active military gets a $5 discount on general admission. If you want shade and a meal, the VIP Canteen Experience runs $204.17 and includes preferred seating, food, and drinks. General parking is free for everyone.

One note: some ticket categories have already shown sold-out status on the advance ticketing sites, so grab yours at pprairshow.org before you head out Saturday morning.

What's your family most excited about — the WWII warbirds or the modern jets?

stories.title: Three Dresser Tip-Over Recalls — FJTJBSI, Gizoon, Alanca (STURDY Act)
stories.angle: CPSC announced three dresser recalls in September's first half — 16,650+ total units. FJTJBSI: ~9,000 units (Amazon, ~$170, Nov 2024–Jul 2026); Gizoon: ~4,396 units (Amazon, May 2025–Aug 2026); Alanca: ~261 units (Wayfair, Apr 2025–Jun 2026). All violate STURDY Act mandatory tip-over standard. Stop using if not wall-anchored. Move away from children's areas.

facebook.long_form:
*Window: 10:00 AM MT*

Important safety alert for Colorado Springs families with young kids: three brands of six-drawer dressers were recalled this month for tip-over and entrapment hazards — and together they add up to more than 16,000 units in homes across the country.

Here's what's been recalled and where they were sold:

🔹 FJTJBSI — about 9,000 units, sold on Amazon.com from November 2024 through July 2026 for around $170. Remedy: write "RECALLED" in permanent marker on the dresser, then email a photo to FJTJBSIrecall@outlook.com for your refund.
🔹 Gizoon — about 4,396 units, sold on Amazon from May 2025 through August 2026 for $138 to $171.
🔹 Alanca — about 261 units, sold on Wayfair from April 2025 through June 2026 for $206 to $240.

All three violate the mandatory federal safety standard under the STURDY Act, which requires dressers to resist tipping when a child climbs or pulls on them.

If you have one of these dressers and it is not currently secured to the wall, stop using it and move it out of any area where children can access it. Full recall details are at cpsc.gov — search the brand name plus "dresser recall."

Have you anchored your kids' dressers to the wall? It's worth double-checking today.

---

stories.angle: D49 Early Childhood Education opened two new preschool classrooms at the D49 Student Success Center (former Falcon Elementary) in August 2026, expanding specialized learning, preschool, and Base49 access. Also: nine more D49 campuses named Colorado Purple Star Schools, recognizing military family support.

facebook.long_form:
*Window: 8:00 AM MT*

Good news for families in District 49: the D49 Student Success Center is open.

Two new early childhood classrooms launched at the start of this school year at the former Falcon Elementary building, expanding the center's capacity for preschool and the Base49 program. The Student Success Center is designed to serve as a hub for specialized learning — a single location where D49's most intensive early childhood and support programs can operate under one roof.

There's more milestone news from D49 this month: nine additional campuses have been named Colorado Purple Star Schools by the Colorado Department of Education, recognizing their exceptional support of military-connected students and families. For a community with significant ties to Fort Carson and Peterson Space Force Base, this recognition matters.

Does your family have a connection to D49? We'd love to hear what the district is doing well in your neighborhood.

stories.title: COS Parks Master Plan Public Comment Closes Sep 22 — Have Your Say
stories.angle: Colorado Springs' Draft Park System Master Plan public comment period is open through September 22, 2026. Plan was presented to Parks Advisory Board Sep 10. PRCS operates 3 community centers, 7 sports complexes, 5 program areas and serves 300,000 residents. Families' input shapes future parks for years. Comment at coloradosprings.gov/ParkSystemMasterPlan.

Colorado Springs families: comment on the Draft Park System Master Plan by Sep 22.

Your input shapes playgrounds, trails, and open spaces for years.

coloradosprings.gov #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
*Window: 12:00 PM MT*

If you've ever pushed a stroller down a cracked trail, wished your neighborhood had a better playground, or wanted more shaded picnic areas at a city park — here's your chance to actually say something about it.

Colorado Springs is in the final stretch of public comments on its Draft Park System Master Plan, and the deadline is September 22. That's six days from today. The plan maps out the city's priorities for parks, trails, and open spaces for years to come, and the Parks Advisory Board reviewed the draft on September 10.

For context on what's at stake: Colorado Springs Parks, Recreation and Cultural Services operates three community centers, seven sports complexes, and five program areas, and serves more than 300,000 residents each year. This master plan will shape how that system grows (or doesn't) over the next decade.

You can read the draft and submit feedback at coloradosprings.gov/ParkSystemMasterPlan. It takes less time than you'd think.

What's the one park feature or trail improvement you most wish Colorado Springs would prioritize?

---

stories.title: Fall Events Roundup — Bark at Briargate, CMZoo Centennial Last Days, Free Movies
stories.angle: Big family week in COS: Bark at Briargate Sep 19 (free, 11 AM–3 PM, dog adoptions + family fun); CMZoo Centennial through Sep 20 (last days — live music, vintage cars); Free outdoor movies every Saturday evening in September/October (Schoolyard series, bring chairs + dogs); Crystal Reservoir/North Slope closes for season Oct 18 — make fall fishing plans now.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
*Window: 3:00 PM MT*

It's a big week for Colorado Springs families, and we've pulled together everything worth knowing about before the weekend:

🐾 **Bark at Briargate** — This Saturday, September 19, from 11 AM to 3 PM. Free admission. Features on-site dog adoptions (great if your family has been thinking about adding a dog), pet-focused vendors, activities, and giveaways. Fun for kids and anyone who loves dogs.

🦒 **CMZoo Centennial — Last Days** — The Colorado Springs Zoo's centennial celebration wraps up September 20. If you haven't made it out for the vintage cars and live music programming, this is your last chance before it closes out. It's included with regular zoo admission.

🎬 **Free Outdoor Movies at the Schoolyard** — Every Saturday evening this month and in October, The Schoolyard hosts free outdoor movies under the stars. Bring your own chairs, dogs are welcome, and there are concessions on site.

🎣 **Last Chance for North Slope Fishing** — The Crystal Reservoir and North Slope Recreation Area closes for fishing season on October 18. If your family fishes, you've got about a month left. Worth a fall weekend trip before the season ends.

What's on your family's calendar this weekend?

---
